status: research-lead; not a transcription of selected 1876 work; not admitted

research_notes.published_translation: Jason Gaiger translation in Charles Harrison and Paul Wood (eds.), Art in Theory 1815–1900 (Blackwell, 1998), pp. 632–635/636; readable legal copy of selected places not yet located.
research_notes.parallel_article: Ortlieb, Kügel and Carbon, Fechner (1866): The Aesthetic Association Principle—A Commented Translation, i-Perception 11(3), 2020, https://doi.org/10.1177/2041669520920309, https://d-nb.info/1269538551/34, CC BY 4.0, pp. 3–4. This translates Fechner 1866, not the 1876 book.
research_notes.fidelity: Terra research reader compared the 1866 facsimile, pp. 179–180, against the selected 1876 places: I p1a is incomplete, I p1b has material differences including laws of being alongside laws of ought in 1866, and I p2 was not found. Do not attribute the 2020 translation to the selected 1876 wording. Independent comparison remains pending.
research_notes.remaining: An author-hosted translation of the 1876 book has now been located, but first place is materially incomplete and terms and independent alignment require review; continue search for a complete source.

book_translation.title: Preschool of Aesthetics, Part I, translated from Fechner 1876

places.I p1a: p. 7; translation omits German definition of aesthetics as the study of what is liked or disliked and the qualification that others call it science of beauty. Not complete alignment.
places.I p1b: pp. 7–8; research reader compared German and English images, semantic content broadly present with several English sentences.
places.I p2: p. 8; research reader compared three corresponding English sentences against German.
